exam.title: Eritrean Secondary Education Certificate Examinations 2025 - Business & Economics (5119)

questions.stem: Movement along the demand curve is due to

options.B: change in the price of substitute.

explanation_steps: A movement along the demand curve occurs only when the price of the specific good (own commodity price) changes. This is called a change in quantity demanded. All other factors (A, B, D, E) cause the entire demand curve to shift.

questions.stem: All are activities in non-financial sector **except**,
explanation_steps: Insurance companies are part of the financial sector because they deal with financial risk, premiums, and capital management. Airlines, textiles, farms, and universities belong to the real (non-financial) economy.

questions.stem: The most direct channel of distribution is from the
explanation_steps: The most direct channel, also known as Level Zero channel, is when the producer sells directly to the final consumer without any middleman (wholesaler, retailer, or agent).

questions.stem: Disposable income is equal to

options.A: gross income less dividend to shareholders.
options.B: net income less personal income tax.
options.D: gross income less personal income tax.

explanation_steps: Disposable income is the amount of money households have left to spend or save after paying personal income taxes. The formula is: $$ DI = PI - \text{Personal Taxes} $$.

questions.stem: In a socialist economic system, there is

options.A: no government control of large enterprises.
options.B: small amount of control of large enterprises.

explanation_steps: Socialism is characterized by state or collective ownership and control of the major means of production (large enterprises and infrastructure), whereas small businesses might sometimes remain in private hands.

questions.stem: Quantity of tomatoes in the market increases with increase in its price. This is explained by the
explanation_steps: The Law of Supply states that there is a direct relationship between price and quantity supplied. As the price of a good rises, producers are willing to offer more of it to the market to increase profit.

questions.stem: Linear $$ 45^0 $$ line of consumption function indicates
explanation_steps: In the Keynesian Cross diagram, the 45-degree line represents points where total spending (consumption) equals total income ($$ Y = C $$). At any point on this line, saving is zero.

questions.stem: If the price of fuel increases and taxi fare increases, then increase in taxi fare is due to
explanation_steps: Fuel is a primary 'input' or cost for providing taxi services. When the price of fuel goes up, the production cost for the taxi driver increases, forcing them to raise the fare to cover these new expenses.

questions.stem: Purchase cost of buildings and vehicles of an enterprise is considered as
explanation_steps: Fixed costs are expenses that do not change with the level of output in the short run. Buildings and vehicles are capital assets; their purchase costs remain the same whether the company produces one unit or a thousand.

questions.stem: Which one is true of complementary goods? They are consumed
explanation_steps: Complementary goods are products that are used together (e.g., car and fuel, bread and butter). An increase in the price of one leads to a decrease in the demand for the other because they are consumed **jointly**.

questions.stem: Points along an indifference curve show equal level of
explanation_steps: By definition, an indifference curve connects all combinations of two goods that provide a consumer with the exact same level of total satisfaction or **utility**. Because utility is the same at every point on the curve, the consumer is 'indifferent' between them.

questions.stem: The amount in the one column sales journal represents

options.A: Debit purchases and Credit Accounts payable.
options.B: Credit purchases and Debit Accounts payable.
options.C: Debit purchases and Debit Accounts payable.
options.D: Debit accounts receivable and Debit sales.
options.E: Debit accounts receivable and Credit sales.

explanation_steps: A one-column sales journal is used exclusively to record sales of merchandise on account (credit sales). The single column represents both a **Debit to Accounts Receivable** and a **Credit to Sales** for the same amount.

questions.stem: The amounts withheld from an employee's gross earnings are recorded by the business as
explanation_steps: When an employer deducts taxes or pension from an employee's salary, that money doesn't belong to the employer. The business is holding it temporarily and owes it to the government or pension fund. Therefore, it is a **liability** until paid.

questions.stem: Who uses accounting information for the purpose of evaluating the business performance and to get timely information in order to assess the company’s strengths and weaknesses?
explanation_steps: Internal users, specifically **Managers**, use detailed accounting data to evaluate performance, make daily decisions, and plan for the future by identifying strengths and weaknesses within the operations.

questions.stem: One of the following is an example of voluntary withholdings.
explanation_steps: Compulsory withholdings (like Income Tax and Pension in Eritrea) are required by law. **Voluntary withholdings** are authorized by the employee, such as voluntary life insurance, health insurance, or charitable contributions.

questions.stem: When a Company uses four special journals and a General journal, credit sales of merchandise are recorded in
explanation_steps: Credit sales of merchandise (selling goods with payment to be received later) are exclusively recorded in the **Sales Journal**. This helps organize transactions and simplifies the posting process to the general ledger.

questions.stem: In accounting, the book of secondary entry refers to
explanation_steps: The Journal is the book of **original entry** (where transactions are first recorded). The **Ledger** is the book of **secondary entry** (or final entry) because it receives data transferred from the journal to categorize it by account.

questions.stem: Mrs. Halima, a government employee, earns a monthly salary of Nakfa 3,000. Her total payroll deduction according to the Eritrean payroll system is Nakfa
explanation_steps:
**Standard Eritrean Payroll (Estimate):** 
- **Pension:** 5% of Basic Salary = $$ 3000 \times 0.05 = 150 $$.
- **Income Tax:** Based on progressive brackets (approx 339 for this level).
- **Total Deduction:** $$ 150 + 339 = 489 $$.

questions.stem: From which account column of the cash receipt journal is a total **not** posted?
explanation_steps: In a Cash Receipts Journal, specialized columns (Cash, Sales, A/R) are posted as a total at the end of the month. The **Sundry** column contains various unrelated accounts, so each item must be posted **individually**; the total of the Sundry column is never posted to a single le

questions.stem: Which of the following is the task of a Bookkeeper?

options.A: Analysing financial activities of the business
options.B: Interpreting financial activities of the business
options.C: Preparing financial statements of the business
options.D: Design accounting system of the business
options.E: Recording financial activities of the business

explanation_steps: Bookkeeping is the routine, clerical part of accounting. Its main task is the **recording** of day-to-day financial transactions in journals and ledgers. Analysis, interpretation, and design are higher-level tasks performed by Accountants.

questions.stem: When a Company uses four special journals and a General journal, borrowing of Nakfa 20,000 at 10% interest from Commercial Bank of Eritrea that will be due in 2 years is recorded in the
explanation_steps: Borrowing money from a bank results in an inflow of cash. In a system using special journals, all transactions involving the receipt of cash are recorded in the **Cash Receipt Journal**.

questions.stem: Which one of the following **does not** require adjusting entry?
explanation_steps: Adjusting entries are made at the end of a period to record internal changes or 'used up' assets (Supplies, Prepaid rent, Inventory) or accrued income. **Cash** balances are adjusted through bank reconciliations, but they do not receive 'adjusting journal entries' in the same way

questions.stem: Which of the following can be recorded in the Purchase journal?

options.A: Credit purchase of machinery for use
options.B: Credit purchase of building for sale
options.D: Withdrawal of cash for personal use

explanation_steps: Note: Actually, the **Purchase Journal** is specifically designed for **Credit purchases of Merchandise Inventory**. Buying machinery (A) on credit goes to General Journal. Cash purchases (C) go to Cash Disbursements. However, in many academic contexts, if 'Merchandise Inventory'

questions.stem: One of the following accounts **is not** a permanent account.
explanation_steps: Permanent (Real) accounts carry their balances over to the next year (Assets, Liabilities, Equity). Temporary (Nominal) accounts like Revenues, Expenses, and **Owner's Drawing** are closed to zero at the end of each year.

questions.stem: The general ledger account from the purchase journal is:
explanation_steps: The Purchase Journal primarily tracks credit purchases. At the end of the month, the total of this journal is posted to the **Accounts Payable** (Credit) and Purchases (Debit) accounts in the General Ledger.

questions.stem: A company uses a Cash journal and a General journal. When it makes partial payment of a liability, the debit amount should be recorded in the
explanation_steps: When a liability (debt) is paid, the Accounts Payable account must be **debited** (to decrease it). If the cash journal has a specific column for Accounts Payable, the amount is placed there.

questions.stem: From the above information, net sales in Nakfa is
explanation_steps:
**Calculation:** 
Net Sales = Sales - (Sales Discounts + Sales Returns and Allowances)
Net Sales = $$ 100,000 - (1,500 + 2,000) $$
Net Sales = $$ 100,000 - 3,500 = 96,500 $$.

questions.stem: From the information above, cost of goods sold in Nakfa is
explanation_steps:
**Calculation:** 
COGS = Beginning Inventory + Net Purchases - Ending Inventory
(Assuming Beginning Inventory = 0 as it's not provided)
COGS = $$ 0 + 50,000 - 12,000 = 38,000 $$.

questions.stem: From the information in the box, net income or net loss is Nakfa
explanation_steps:

Net Income = Net Sales - COGS - Operating Expenses
Net Income = $$ 96,500 (Q27) - 38,000 (Q28) - (3,000 + 4,500) $$

questions.stem: The difference between the two sides of an account is referred to as
explanation_steps: An account has two sides (Debit and Credit). The difference between the total of the debit side and the total of the credit side is the **account balance**.

questions.stem: When a Company uses four special journals and a General journal, purchase discounts should be recorded in the
explanation_steps: Purchase discounts are taken when a company pays its creditors within the discount period. Since this involves a cash outflow, the transaction is recorded in the **Cash Payments (Disbursements) Journal**, which typically has a specific column for purchase discounts.

questions.stem: Which of the following **is true** when a company deposits cash in the bank?

options.C: Depositor’s balance in the chequing account decrease.
options.D: Depositor’s balance in the ledger account decrease.
options.E: The bank debits the company’s chequing account.

explanation_steps: From the bank's perspective, a customer's deposit is a **liability** because the bank owes that money back to the customer. Therefore, when a company deposits cash, the bank's liability increases (recorded as a credit on the bank's books).

questions.stem: Which of the following **is incorrect** concerning the practices of control over cash receipts and disbursements?

options.A: Put all cash receipts in the bank daily.
options.B: Verify all cash sales using cash register tape and sales invoices.
options.C: Assign different persons for cash receipts and cash disbursements.
options.D: Establish a petty cash fund for large cash payments.

explanation_steps: A **Petty Cash Fund** is specifically established for **small (minor) payments** like stamps, office supplies, or taxi fares where writing a check is impractical. Large payments should always be made by check for better control.

questions.stem: One of the following **is not** a possible fraud of the payroll system.
explanation_steps: Payroll fraud involves stealing money from the company, such as creating 'ghost' employees (A), keeping ex-employees on payroll (B), or paying for time not worked (D). **Decreasing pay rates** is typically an administrative decision or an error, not a fraudulent scheme used by a

options.D: credit cash over and short by Nakfa 10.
options.E: debit cash over and short by Nakfa 10.

Receipts ($$ 375 $$) + Remaining Cash ($$ 115 $$) = $$ 490 $$.
**Step 2: Compare to original fund.** 
Original Fund ($$ 500 $$) - Accounted Funds ($$ 490 $$) = $$ 10 $$ missing.
**Step 3: Journalize.** 
Since money is missing, we **debit Ca

questions.stem: If interest rates rise the amount of
explanation_steps: The interest rate represents the cost of borrowing money. When interest rates rise, borrowing becomes more expensive for businesses, leading them to delay or cancel projects. Therefore, total **investment spending falls**.

questions.stem: The method of depreciation which is based on the assumption that depreciation is solely the result of use and that the passage of time plays no role in the depreciation process is
explanation_steps: The **Units of Production** (or Units of Activity) method ignores time. It calculates depreciation based on actual usage (miles driven, hours used, units produced). If a machine is not used for a month, no depreciation is recorded under this method.

questions.stem: On January 2, 2023 Zara Company purchased land for a new retail operation. It pays (all payments in Nakfa) a net purchase price of 400,000; brokerage fees of 20,000; legal fees of 15,000; tearing down old building 150,000; receiving 50,000 residual from the old building, and grading fees of 60,000. The cost of land is Nakfa
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Sum all necessary costs to prepare land.**
- Purchase Price: $$ 400,000 $$
- Brokerage: $$ 20,000 $$
- Legal: $$ 15,000 $$
- Net Demolition: $$ 150,000 - 50,000 = 100,000 $$
- Grading: $$ 60,000 $$
**Step 2: Total.** 
$$ 400 + 20 + 15 + 100 + 60 = 595,000 $$.

questions.stem: An economy can grow over time due to increase in
explanation_steps: Economic growth is characterized by an increase in the capacity of an economy to produce goods and services. This is driven by **increases in labor productivity** (A) and results in an **increase in national income** (B). Price level increases (C) represent inflation, not growth.

questions.stem: A machine that costs Nakfa 100,000 and has a book value of Nakfa 5,000 is sold for Nakfa 15,000. The entry to record the sale results in
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Calculate Gain/Loss.** 
Sale Price ($$ 15,000 $$) - Book Value ($$ 5,000 $$) = **$$ 10,000 $$ Gain**. 
**Step 2: Rule.** 
A gain on sale is always recorded as a **Credit** because it increases equity.

questions.stem: Which of the following **is not** a macroeconomic problem?
explanation_steps: Macroeconomics deals with the economy as a whole (GDP, total unemployment, national inflation). The price of a specific good, like **potatoes**, is a **microeconomic** issue because it concerns an individual market.

questions.stem: Value of intermediate goods are subtracted in calculating GDP because

options.A: they are not used for further processing.
options.B: it is less important in production.
options.C: it is important to avoid double counting.

explanation_steps: Intermediate goods are materials used to produce final goods. If we counted the value of flour AND the bread made from it, the flour would be counted twice. We subtract them to **avoid double counting** and accurately measure the economy's output.

questions.stem: Goods and services bought by households are part of
explanation_steps: In the expenditure approach to GDP, spending by individuals and households on final goods and services (like food, clothes, and haircuts) is categorized as **consumption expenditure** ($$ C $$).

questions.stem: Other things being equal, if an increase in the price of oranges increases the demand for papaya, then the commodities are
explanation_steps: Substitutes are goods that can be used in place of each other. If oranges become expensive, consumers switch to a cheaper alternative like papaya, causing the demand for papaya to rise.

questions.stem: Which industry is close to oligopoly market structure?
explanation_steps: An oligopoly is a market dominated by a **few large firms**. The aircraft industry (e.g., Boeing and Airbus) is a classic example because only a very small number of companies produce commercial airplanes globally due to high entry costs.

questions.stem: In a mixed economic system, resources are allocated through
explanation_steps: A mixed economy combines elements of both market (private) and command (government) systems. Resources are distributed through both **private market interactions** and **government planning/regulation**.

questions.stem: Property that is considered as a security for a loan is referred to as
explanation_steps: **Collateral** is an asset (like a house, car, or land) that a borrower offers to a lender as a guarantee. If the borrower fails to pay the loan, the lender can seize the collateral to recover the money.

questions.stem: If a country produces only wheat and it exports wheat to import cloth then it
explanation_steps: Specialization occurs when a country focuses its resources on producing a limited range of goods. If it produces **only** one item (wheat), it has **completely specialized** in that product to gain efficiency and trade for other needs.

questions.stem: An amount paid to insurance company for a policy is called
explanation_steps: A **premium** is the periodic payment made by an individual or business to an insurance company to keep an insurance policy active and cover future risks.

questions.stem: Gross National Product (GNP) minus depreciation equals
explanation_steps:
**Formula:** $$ NNP = GNP - \text{Depreciation} $$. 
Net National Product (NNP) measures the total value of goods and services produced by a nation's citizens minus the value of the capital used up (worn out) during production.

questions.stem: When revenue is greater than expenditure in the government budget, there is
explanation_steps: A government budget is in **surplus** when the total tax revenues collected exceed the total government spending (expenditure) during a specific period.

questions.stem: Which of the following **is not** true of paper money (Nakfa) in Eritrea?

options.B: It is a medium of exchange.
options.E: It is a store of value.

explanation_steps: Paper money (currency) is physically fragile and **does deteriorate** over time due to handling, moisture, and wear and tear. All other options are defining functions and characteristics of the Nakfa.

questions.stem: As income increases demand for a commodity falls, then the commodity is
explanation_steps: An **inferior good** is a type of good whose demand decreases as the consumer's income rises. People switch from inferior goods (e.g., public transport, low-quality food) to higher-quality substitutes (Normal/Luxury goods) when they can afford them.

questions.stem: An example of a Mortgage Bank in Eritrea is

options.C: Housing and Saving Bank of Eritrea.

explanation_steps: The **Housing and Saving Bank of Eritrea (HSBE)** functions as a specialized financial institution that provides long-term loans specifically for construction and housing (mortgages).

questions.stem: Assets that are easily convertible into cash are referred to as
explanation_steps: **Liquid assets** are cash on hand or assets that can be sold very quickly for cash with little or no loss in value. Cash itself is the most liquid asset, followed by bank deposits and short-term securities.

questions.stem: Conflict between management and owners of a business enterprise is common in
explanation_steps: This is known as the **Principal-Agent Problem**. In **corporations**, there is a clear separation between ownership (stockholders) and control (managers). Managers may sometimes act in their own self-interest rather than maximizing the owners' profits, leading to conflict.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **correct** about capital investment of a firm?

options.A: In the short run, there is no fixed capital.
options.B: In the long run, there is no variable capital.
options.C: In the short run, there is no variable capital.
options.D: In the long run, there is no fixed capital.

explanation_steps: In the **long run**, all factors of production are variable. A firm has enough time to expand its factory, buy new land, or change any 'fixed' input. Therefore, there is no fixed capital in the long run; everything can be changed.

questions.stem: The theory of comparative advantage is related to
explanation_steps: While Adam Smith introduced Absolute Advantage, **David Ricardo** developed the **Theory of Comparative Advantage** in the early 19th century. It suggests that trade is beneficial even if one country is less efficient at everything, as long as it specializes in what it is *relati

questions.stem: For which of the following does a Company debit accounts receivable in adjusting entries related to Bank Reconciliation statement?

options.A: The bank collected Nakfa 1,000 on behalf of the Company.
options.B: A deposit for Nakfa 500 made late on May 31 does not appear on the bank statement.
options.C: A customer’s cheque for Nakfa 2,500 is returned marked NSF.
options.D: Cheques written by the Company which have not been cleared by the bank.

explanation_steps: When a customer's check is returned as NSF (Non-Sufficient Funds), the company must reverse the initial entry where they thought they received cash. They **debit Accounts Receivable** to put the debt back on the customer's record and credit Cash to reduce the book balance.

questions.stem: One of the following is **not** true concerning the Eritrean payroll system?

options.A: The amount recorded as salary and wages expense is the sum of the gross pay amounts for all employees.
options.B: The contractual amount which an employee earns during a pay period is referred to as gross earnings.
options.C: The rate of the pension fund of the State of Eritrea is 5% of basic salary.
options.D: The journal entry for the net amount paid to employees involves a credit to salaries and wages payable.
options.E: Salaried employees earn a fixed amount each pay period.

explanation_steps: Option D is incorrect because the final payment entry involves a **debit** to Salaries and Wages Payable (to close the liability) and a **credit to Cash** (money leaving the business). Crediting the liability would imply the debt is increasing.

questions.stem: A bank issues debit memorandum when it

options.D: adds interest revenue to the depositor’s account.

explanation_steps: To a bank, a customer's deposit is a liability (Credit balance). Therefore, when the bank wants to **decrease** your account (for service charges, NSF checks, etc.), it 'debits' your account. This is communicated via a debit memorandum.

questions.stem: Mr. Abraham is an employee of Asmara Textile Factory. His basic wage rate is Nakfa 30 per hour for a 48 normal working hours per week. His overtime rate is 1.5 his normal rate. Mr. Abraham worked 55 hours during the week. His **net pay** according to the Eritrean payroll system is Nakfa
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Calculate Gross Pay.**
- Regular Pay (48 hrs): $$ 48 \times 30 = 1,440 $$.
- Overtime Hours: $$ 55 - 48 = 7 \text{ hrs} $$.
- Overtime Rate: $$ 30 \times 1.5 = 45 \text{/hr} $$.
- Overtime Pay: $$ 7 \times 45 = 315 $$.
- **Total Gross:** $$ 1,440 + 315 = 1,755 $$.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is cross-referencing between the journal and a ledger?

options.A: Amounts on the debit side of a journal are transferred to the debit side of the ledger account.
options.B: Amounts on the credit side of a journal are transferred to the credit side of the ledger account.
options.C: Writing the date column of the journal entry in the date column of the ledger account.
options.D: Writing page number of the journal in the post reference column of the ledger account.

explanation_steps: Cross-referencing (or posting) is the process of moving journal data to the ledger. It includes transferring amounts (A, B), dates (C), and crucially, recording reference numbers (D) so an auditor can trace a number from the ledger back to its original journal entry.

questions.stem: One of the following accounting activities is optional.
explanation_steps: A **worksheet** is an internal tool used by accountants to organize data for adjusting and closing entries. While very helpful, it is not a mandatory part of the formal accounting records or financial statements. Journals and ledgers are essential requirements.

options.C: Misplacing a debit balance in the credit column of the account or credit balance in the debit column of the account.
options.D: A debit to Accounts receivable is recorded as a debit to cash.

options.B: Increase in capital by Nakfa 75,000 but no change in total assets.

Option D describes a valid balance ($$ +75 = +75 + 0 $

questions.stem: All points on the production possibility curve indicate
explanation_steps: The Production Possibilities Curve (PPC) represents the maximum potential output of an economy. Any point **on the line** indicates that all resources are being used fully and efficiently. Points inside are inefficient, and points outside are currently impossible.

options.A: Depreciation expense and Accumulated depreciation overstated
options.B: Fixed assets and Accumulated depreciation understated
options.C: Depreciation expense overstated, Fixed assets no change
options.D: Depreciation expense understated, Fixed assets overstated
options.E: Fixed assets and Depreciation expense overstated

explanation_steps:
If the entry (Debit Depreciation Expense; Credit Accumulated Depreciation) is not made: 
1. **Depreciation Expense** is ignored, so expenses are **understated**. 
2. **Accumulated Depreciation** (a contra-asset) is not increased, so the net value of **Fixed Assets** on the balanc

questions.stem: Net exports are negative when
explanation_steps:
**Formula:** $$ \text{Net Exports} = \text{Exports} - \text{Imports} $$. 
If the value of imports is higher than exports, the result is a negative number, also known as a **trade deficit**.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is an addition or new investment in GDP?

options.B: Purchase of milk by dairy factory
options.E: Purchase of new vehicle by a restaurant

explanation_steps: In GDP, **Investment ($$ I $$)** refers to the purchase of new capital goods (machinery, tools, buildings) that will be used to produce future goods. A restaurant buying a **new vehicle** is a capital investment. Milk (B) is an intermediate good, and Welfare (A) is a transfer pay

questions.stem: If income increases from 500 Nakfa to 600 Nakfa and saving increases from 100 Nakfa to 150 Nakfa, then the Marginal Propensity to Save (MPS) is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Find change in Income ($$ \Delta Y $$).** 
$$ 600 - 500 = 100 $$.
**Step 2: Find change in Saving ($$ \Delta S $$).** 
$$ 150 - 100 = 50 $$.
**Step 3: Calculate MPS.** 
$$ MPS = \Delta S / \Delta Y = 50 / 100 = 0.50 $$.

questions.stem: Analysis of consumer behavior is based on
explanation_steps: Economists analyze how consumers choose what to buy using **Marginal Utility Theory**. This theory suggests that consumers aim to maximize their total utility (satisfaction) within their budget constraints.

questions.stem: All are considered as withdrawals from the circular flow of income and expenditure **except**,
explanation_steps: **Withdrawals (Leakages)** are diversions of money from the main spending flow: Savings ($$ S $$), Taxes ($$ T $$), and Imports ($$ M $$). **Investment ($$ I $$)** is an **Injection**, as it adds money into the circular flow.

questions.stem: If income increases by 25% and demand for meat increases by 40%, then income elasticity of demand is
explanation_steps:
**Formula:** $$ E_y = rac{\% \Delta Q_d}{\% \Delta Y} $$
**Calculation:** $$ 40\% / 25\% = 1.60 $$. 
Since $$ E_y > 1 $$, meat is considered a luxury (or normal, income-elastic) good in this context.
